Well, the one major problem with a domain of our own, means we combat spammers.

 

It was going OK, but last night we got hit hard by a spam bot creation, and had over 10000 script executions, our daily limit. The site wont be affected until we hit 150% then it would be temporarily shut down for the day for exceeding limits.

 

Well, thats not good that its spam doing that. So I shut off account creation. There is a note on the front page on how to create an account ont he Wiki if you want one.

 

In other news, if anyone has the time and motivation, please contact me to discuss becoming a mod on the wiki to help clean that stuff up, and to be available to create new accounts.

posts.name: lynkfox
posts.cooked:
In the battle against SPAM on the wiki, the following manuevers have been performed.

 

 

Play: Disable Account Creation - For the time being, all accounts can only be created by Admins. At the time of this post, that is Lynkfox and Powerhound (Sonvar), but UMX will be joining those ranks as soon as the site is back up.

 

Power: CAPTCHA! I thought I enabled it. The settings are all there.... except the one that tells the wiki to run the captcha script.... *headslam* well, ok. Thats been added. It is set for the time being as edits all require a captcha to process, but we are using the new google reCaptcha - which is, for the most part, invisible if you are already proven to google. You may or may not see it. We'll see how much it helps

 

Draw: New attempt: dns spam blacklisting, through a honeypot - I've enabled the DNS blacklist, which runs whenever an edit is made, and if the address of the editor is on a DNS honeypot blacklist, then it returns a 403/forbidden. 

 

 

When the site comes back up we'll see how that helps, and go about cleaning up the crap from the spambots. 

 

If any users experience difficulties in editing the site, let me know.  Honestly, the account creation disable is something I don't want, because it means a lot of extra work for moderators of the wiki, plus a lot of waiting for the people involved. But it is the first line of defense, because spam bots/users won't attempt to contact any of us to get an account created. However, hundreds upon hundreds of accounts were created last night, and not all of them have been blocked. They can still edit pages until they are blocked, and will be a potential threat - hence the captcha and the dns blacklisting.  Hopefully we'll get through cleaning up the site, and then move on and be able to remove a few of the restrictions (the account creation is the one I'm hoping for... but feel like it is a lost cause)

 

Such is the world we live in on the internet. 

 

When the site comes back up, in the morning I'll be adding a bit to the front page to direct potential new wiki users to this thread for processing of a new account.
